svg.title: Compact extraction in the atomic standard-measure branch
svg.desc: A countable measurable point code on a conull subspace makes a measure atom a positive singleton. Quasi-invariance, freeness and ergodicity give one conull countable orbit. A positive Borel set contains an actual point of that orbit; its singleton is compact and misses every nonidentity translate. The atomless branch remains open.

g.text: From a measure atom to a compact singleton
Finite standard measure · quasi-invariant ergodic action · every point has trivial stabilizer
A is a measure atom, μ(A) > 0.
S is conull; Bₙ separates its points.
Choose the full-mass side Cₙ of each Bₙ.
2. The point remains in the original space
3. One countable orbit is conull — Theorem 3.5
D = {y : μ({y}) > 0} is countable and invariant; ergodicity makes it conull.
The free orbit map G → D, g ↦ gx₀, is injective. Therefore G is countable.
O = Gx₀ is Borel, invariant and nonnull; ergodicity makes this single orbit conull.
4. Extract inside the actual positive Borel set E
Choose x ∈ E ∩ O. Then L = {x} is compact, μ(L) > 0, and gL ∩ L = ∅ for g ≠ e.
The same L works for every nonidentity element, hence for every compact parameter family.
Corollary 3.6: the remaining standard-measure compact-extraction question is atomless.
Proof: Borel carriers and uniform wandering neighborhoods, Lemma 3.4 / Theorem 3.5 / Corollary 3.6.
